gaps.sentence: 'Could you open the window?' she asked. She asked me ___ the window.
gaps.explanation: 'Could you...?' requests are reported with ask + object + to-infinitive; no could remains.

gaps.sentence: 'Don't leave your belongings unattended,' the announcement repeated. The announcement ___ passengers not to leave their belongings unattended.
gaps.hint: warn sb not to do sth
gaps.explanation: The warning fits warn + object + not to + infinitive.

gaps.sentence: 'You must be joking!' I exclaimed. I exclaimed that he ___ be joking.
gaps.hint: must of deduction does not backshift
gaps.explanation: Must expressing confident deduction usually stays must; only obligation shifts to had to.

gaps.sentence: 'I'll be waiting outside the cinema,' he said. He said he ___ waiting outside the cinema.
gaps.explanation: will be + -ing becomes would be + -ing in reported speech.

gaps.sentence: 'I'll have finished by noon,' she promised. She promised she ___ finished by noon.
gaps.explanation: will have + past participle becomes would have + past participle.

gaps.sentence: 'We're leaving here at dawn,' they said. They said they were leaving ___ at dawn.
gaps.explanation: Place adverbs shift with the speaker's perspective: here → there.

gaps.sentence: She ___ that the storm had passed.
gaps.explanation: Without a personal object, use said (that)...; told requires an object.

gaps.sentence: 'Please, please don't leave me,' he sobbed. He begged her ___ leave him.
gaps.hint: beg sb not to do sth
gaps.explanation: Negative begging: begged her not to leave; the negative precedes the infinitive.
